query: For nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts used in ethanol oxidation, strong reported performance has not yet yielded a comprehensive causal understanding of catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability under reaction conditions. Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis explaining what governs one of these behaviors and why. Specify an unnamed controlled change and an appropriate baseline, the predicted observations relative to that baseline, the operating boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Epitaxially depositing a thin, controlled layer of a FeCoNi–platinum-group-metal high-entropy alloy on nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts will modify the surface electronic structure at the core‐shell interface, reducing catalyst poisoning and thereby enhancing durability and selectivity during ethanol oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst particles without any additional surface treatment.
generation.intervention: Apply an epitaxial deposition to form a thin FeCoNi–platinum-group-metal high-entropy alloy shell on the catalyst particles.
generation.conditions: Conduct ethanol oxidation under standard electrochemical reaction conditions (controlled temperature, pressure, ethanol concentration, and potential) where the untreated catalysts have been previously characterized.
generation.structural_mediator: The well-defined core–shell interface that alters the local d-band electronic structure of the catalyst surface.
generation.mechanism: The deposited high-entropy alloy shell adjusts the adsorption energies of reaction intermediates by tuning the catalyst’s surface electronic states. This modification is expected to mitigate the accumulation of poisoning species and favor reaction pathways that enhance selectivity and durability during ethanol oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated catalysts, the coated catalysts will exhibit a measurable improvement in durability (longer operational lifetime with less deactivation) and an enhanced selectivity for ethanol oxidation—with higher current density for the desired reaction pathway and reduced formation of unwanted byproducts.
generation.baseline: Catalysts identical in composition and preparation except for the absence of the epitaxial high-entropy alloy shell.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected under ethanol oxidation conditions where the shell remains stable (moderate temperatures and pressures typical of standard electrocatalytic setups) and where the deposition technique yields a uniform, adherent coating without inducing significant interdiffusion at the core–shell interface.
generation.uncertainty: While the qualitative improvement is anticipated based on surface electronic modifications, the precise magnitude of durability and selectivity enhancement and the exact electronic shifts at the interface remain to be established through operando measurements.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts: one group with the epitaxial deposition of the FeCoNi–platinum-group-metal high-entropy alloy shell and one group without any surface modification. Subject both groups to ethanol oxidation in a controlled electrochemical cell, while monitoring their catalytic performance over time via operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and electrochemical measurements.
measurements: Product selectivity analysis (via chromatographic or spectroscopic methods)
Operando XAS to monitor electronic state changes at the interface
Comparison of any catalyst deactivation behaviors
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated catalysts do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in durability (i.e., similar deactivation rates) and ethanol oxidation selectivity (i.e., similar product distributions and current densities) relative to the untreated baseline under identical conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
